name: Global Botanic Garden Fund
summary: Set of small grants for botanic gardens, especially under-resourced ones in high-biodiversity areas, to drive plant conservation projects; each grant has its own purpose and eligibility.
reporting: A final report on completion: short narrative on outcomes, photos and videos where applicable, and an itemised budget against actual spending.

eligibility.rule: For member-only grants, is a BGCI Member Institution or pays membership before disbursement
For ArbNet grants, partners form a partnership between two botanical institutions
For ArbNet grants, at least one partner is accredited or applies by the closing date
For LLNPP grants, is based in the Caribbean or Central American region, including Mexico
For LLNPP grants, holds permanent ex situ living collections
For GSC grants, includes at least 2 species shared and banked at BGSV
For GSC grants, incorporates at least one new accession into the institution's seed bank
For GSC grants, includes only seeds with confirmed orthodox storage properties

status.quote: Apply to the GBGF Member, ArbNet, MLA, LLNPP and GSC Grants are now closed for 2026.

access.quote: BGCI issues a call for application once per year per grant.

window.quote: BGCI issues a call for application once per year per grant.

amount.quote: Each grant awarded ranges from USD$750-10,000 (depending on the grant chosen).

reporting.quote: Successful grants will be required to submit a final report upon completion of the project with the following information: A short narrative report describing the outcome of the project using the method of evaluating described in the application Photos and videos where applicable An itemised budget vs actual

effort.quote: The BGCI Global Botanic Garden Fund grant application will require the following information:

eligibility.quote: The BGCI Member Grants are open to BGCI Member Institutions only. Botanic Gardens that are not members may apply, but a membership fee must be paid before the grant is disbursed.
Involve a partnership between two botanical institutions (arboretum, botanic garden, public garden, etc.).
At least one of the two partners must be an ArbNet accredited arboretum (accreditation applications may be submitted by the closing date of the Global Botanic Garden Fund).

Grants are available only for institutions based in the Caribbean and Central American region as defined by the Caribbean and Central American Botanic Gardens Network (please note Mexico is included).
We invite applications from botanic gardens, arboreta and botanical institutions that hold permanent ex situ living collections (as defined per GardenSearch).
Projects must include at least 2 species that will be shared and banked at BGSV.
There must be at least one new accession incorporated into your institution's seed bank as part of this project.
Only seeds with known and confirmed orthodox storage properties can be included in project proposals.
